title: Async iterators (for await…of)
description: Async iterables expose `[Symbol.asyncIterator]` and let `for await...of` consume values that arrive over time.

notes: `for await...of` is ONLY valid inside an `async` function (or top-level module).
`[Symbol.asyncIterator]` is a DIFFERENT well-known symbol from `[Symbol.iterator]` — don't mix them up.
`next()` returns a Promise that resolves to `{ value, done }` — the wrapper, not the value, is async.

questions.q: What does an async iterator's `next()` return?
questions.explain: The Promise wraps the whole result record, not just the item — `for await...of` awaits it, then reads `.value` and `.done` off the settled object.

options: Only inside an async function or top-level module
questions.explain: It needs an await-capable scope — inside a plain function it's a SyntaxError, which is why the reference wraps the loop in an `(async () => { ... })()` IIFE.

questions.q: Which well-known symbol does `for await...of` look up FIRST when iterating an object?
options: Symbol.iterator — async iteration just awaits each sync value
Symbol.asyncIterator on the returned iterator, not the iterable itself
questions.explain: `for await...of` asks the iterable for `[Symbol.asyncIterator]` first, and only falls back to `[Symbol.iterator]` (awaiting each yielded value) when it's absent. `Symbol.for('asyncIterator')` is an unrelated registry symbol — not equal to `Symbol.asyncIterator`.

questions.q: What happens if you use `for...of` (no await) on an object with only `[Symbol.asyncIterator]`?
options: It works, JS auto-awaits each value
It logs Promises instead of values
It throws after the first iteration
questions.explain: Sync `for...of` looks up `[Symbol.iterator]`, which isn't defined here.
